The game is very good.

As of the time of writing this review, I've been working on beating the game on the Bro difficulty after beating it on easy.

The main complaints I might have about the game are as follows: 
[list]
[*]All enemies seem to have square hitboxes, though very few, some projectiles and enemies don't perfectly match it. 
[*]Having a simple restart button would be nice. In some cases I am far in a level and know that I won't reach the end so I have to keep getting hit by enemies to restart. Going to the map and back into the level also plays cutscenes again. making it not ideal.
[*]The story can have some odd moments that might not have aged well, (mild cringe and cutscenes cannot be skipped), but then again it's YouTubers from over a decade ago and not all of the cutscenes are too drawn out. ([spoiler]Except for the ending moon one with Cryatonic.[/spoiler]) The voice acting makes it seem like everyone was recorded separately and makes the conversations seem odd.
[*]The second difficultly, Hard, seems unnecessary, most players would likely either play Easy or Bro, Easy for casual players and Bro for those who want a challenge. Why play on Hard when playing on Bro would be more rewarding?
[*]A timer would be nice so that players could more easily share how fast they can complete the levels. I found several tricks where small waiting sections of the level can be skipped and competing for times would be nice.
[*]There is a softlock on one level.[spoiler] On the Rhino Desert Platforming level, skipping over one of the rhinos causes the game to move the camera forward. but no enemies/obstacles appear and progress is halted until death or level exit.[/spoiler]
[/list]

Overall the game is good, the main reasons why are as follows:
[list]
[*]The controls are great. I played this on the Steam Deck and had no issues. (Though I remember having issues back when I played this on my phone, but that seems more like the nature of touchscreen controls than an issue with the game.)
[*]Effort was put in to make the game very replayable. From collecting Patches, unlocking characters/abilities, playing the game on [spoiler]Pug Mode, as if Bro wasn't hard enough[/spoiler], and even some holiday themed additional levels.
[*]The gameplay is great. Some small details show how great the effort for this was. For example, [spoiler]during the final boss, breaking many of the barrels to get a bouncer platform is technically not required. With a good timed bounce off of a barrel or Markiplier's flying power, the boss can be hit early.[/spoiler]
[*]Coins seem hard to farm, [spoiler]however the snowy level [i]Hurry Up![/i] makes it otherwise. Just run the level on Bro difficulty and collect coins. Fast completion with ~200 coins per level play.[/spoiler]
[*]Many of the patches are genuinely well hidden and fun to find. I only had to look up the location of one. [spoiler]Halloween level, you'll likely know which one it is after playing it.[/spoiler]
[/list]

Overall I highly recommend the game. I got the game on discount for ~$1.59. Even at full price, I would highly recommend the game. (SteamDB for users who don't want to pay full price for a game that came out a decade ago: https://steamdb.info/app/390520/)

Este es un juego que le tengo mucho cariño. Lo compré en Steam en el 2016 y lo jugué sin parar hasta que me lo pasé. En el 2020 lo volví a jugar para recordar y pues ahorita en el 2026 decidí pasármelo en modo difícil (modo bro). El juego está super bien hecho y tiene un pixel art que está muy bien hecho y es una carta de amor al humor y la personalidad que PewDiePie tenia por allá en el 2015. Sentí bastante nostalgia al escuchar los chistes y diálogos de aquella época.

Lo único que no me gustó del juego es que las dificultades son muy diferentes la una de la otra. El modo fácil y el normal son exageradamente fáciles: los enemigos solo te quitan 1 corazón por ataque y hay bastantes puntos de guardado. Sin embargo, en el modo bro (modo difícil rojo) te toca pasarte el nivel de corrido y los enemigos te quitan los 4 corazones por ataque. Ese modo me costó bastante en pasarlo. Para terminar con el tema de las dificultades, el modo pug (el modo más difícil del juego) te pone a jugar con las dificultad del modo bro, pero con una sola vida. Ya me parece exageradamente difícil jugar en esa dificultad. Obviamente no la van a cambiar, pero me hubiera gustado que ajustarán mejor las dificultades. 

Si fuiste un fan de PewDiePie en la época 2012-2015, te recomiendo jugarlo para recordar el humor que él tenia en esos momentos; y para ser un juego de un Youtuber, me pareció bastante bueno.

This delightful little arcade game is full of funny and creative ideas, reminiscent of Angry Nerd games but with a lighter, sillier vibe and no offensive language. You play as a blogger on a mission to reclaim stolen fans from the Barrel King, who wants to keep all the thumb up for your videos to himself.

The enemies are mostly hopping barrels, some can shoot lasers or fly or divide into 2 smaller barrels once being hit. Your character wields attack and defense skills, my favorite attack ability is the sword that spins around you, hurting any enemy that gets close, with defense skill as a clock freezes time, letting you slip past enemies with ease.

Game map and enemies are well varied. Like in South Africa you ride and jumps on rhinos, dodge suicidal tiger sharks with bombs, and face a sniper rifle giraffe boss in the end. At the North Pole levels, you pass slippery ice, avoiding seals and exploding cows while rescuing a trapped whale. Later, you’ll encounter aliens, werewolves, bats, and even a T-Rex in a subway station with Slender Man trying to nab you... Those wild mixes of bizarre yet funny ideas work out fine.

You’ll usually have enough hearts (up to 16 when maxed out) to reach checkpoints, however, falling off the screen is an instant game over unless you have an animal friend with you. Since the game demands precise jumps, it is not uncommon to restart a level especially in special festival levels like Halloween, Christmas, and Valentine. These themed levels are nice crafted but the Valentine level is frustratingly tough. Thankfully these are optional levels, you can complete the main game without them.

For a 2015 release, PewDiePie holds up well in 2025. The creativity makes it a joy to play.

A lot better than expected. I did mute the voice-lines immediately however, which might've led me to enjoy the game much more than intended. Translavania and Abandoned Station are RNG messes of levels and overally incredibly not fun to a level that feels inexcusable. Most situations in those levels do not feel like the player was at fault and you have to survive 3 whole minutes. It becomes a massive slog. And so does the final boss of the game, which has some incredibly boring/easy phases early on and lasts for WAAAAY too long. Very not fun especially for a no-hit, before that boss I had 14 hours in and finished at 19 hours.

Overall, I think this is a fun platformer game (when voicelines are off) but I don't think I would recommend beating all levels on pug mode unless you are hell-bent on 100%ing steam games. Was overall a really fun 100% if it wasn't for those 3 levels :/

[b]Beginning[/b]
I used to watch PewDiePie videos every day, so I clearly remember when this game was first announced. I really wanted to play it back then, but it wasn’t free, and eventually I forgot about it.
Seven years later, I randomly found it again on Steam by accident. I bought it, and it sat in my backlog collecting dust for three years. Then, one day, I finally played it. Due to the sheer amount of dust accumulated over time, I sneezed the moment I launched it. Random fact but I remembered it while writing this review.

[b]The PewDiePie Universe Theory [/b]
Since the game is based on the real-life personality PewDiePie and how he sees the world, and because some elements in the game are impossible in our reality, we can theorize that there are two universes: our own, and the “PewDiePie Universe.”
Most likely, PewDiePie is the only entity who can fully experience the PewDiePie Universe, but fortunately, we’re able to get a glimpse of it by playing this game. So with that explained, let’s move on.

[b]Stage 11: Hidden Meanings?[/b]
In the very beginning of Stage 11, "Mines Entrance," you receive a phone call from Marzia telling you she wants to see “Orange is the New Bro.” This tells us that there's a show called Orange is the New Bro in the PewDiePie Universe.
The game was released in 2015. The closest equivalent in our universe is Orange Is the New Black, which was released in 2013. Considering development time, this reference lines up well.
From this discovery, we can conclude that “bro” in the PewDiePie Universe is “black” in our own. 
This becomes more significant when thinking about the 2017 incident on the bridge (you know the one). PewDiePie used the word “bro,” a term he commonly uses to refer to his fans.

With only facts and reasoning, we’ve reached this conclusion. And as a scientist, it was my duty to make this information public.
